name: Atheist feminism
summary: Atheist feminism combines feminism with atheism, holding that religion is a major source of women's oppression and that most religions are sexist. It traces to nineteenth-century freethinkers such as Ernestine Rose, Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Matilda Joslyn Gage, and today also challenges sexism inside secular and atheist movements. Its core commitments are women's legal equality, reproductive rights, and strict separation of church and state.
scope: The mainstream atheist and secular feminist tradition from Stanton's Woman's Bible (1895) and Gage's Woman, Church and State (1893) to the Freedom From Religion Foundation (Anne Nicol Gaylor, Annie Laurie Gaylor) and modern figures such as Taslima Nasrin and Sikivu Hutchinson. It excludes religious and 'spiritual' feminisms. The sources are about religion, sex and law, so most economic, defence and technology answers are low-confidence inferences from the movement's progressive, rights-based outlook.

keyFigures.name: Elizabeth Cady Stanton
keyFigures.role: Suffragist who edited The Woman's Bible and argued that the Bible degrades women.

keyFigures.name: Matilda Joslyn Gage
keyFigures.role: Author of Woman, Church and State (1893) and advocate of separating church and state.

keyFigures.name: Anne Nicol Gaylor
keyFigures.role: Co-founder of the Freedom From Religion Foundation and abortion rights activist who saw religion as the root of women's oppression.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Inferred: mainstream secular feminists back public healthcare, and Gaylor's abortion funding work shows concern for women unable to pay for care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from mainstream feminist concern with low-paid women's work; the sources do not discuss wage policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Inferred: feminism in this tradition emphasises structural disadvantage that markets alone do not correct, though the sources are silent on economics.

public-ownership.rationale: The sources never address ownership of industry, and adherents range from liberals to socialists.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the progressive-left leaning of modern secular feminists; not discussed in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from general feminist support for organised labour; sources do not address it.

property-fundamental.rationale: Gage and Stanton attacked laws giving husbands control of wives' property, but nothing here treats property as an overriding right; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from the left-liberal alignment of modern atheist feminists; not addressed in the sources.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred: welfare cuts fall disproportionately on women and feminists generally oppose them.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split between liberal and socialist views.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from civil-libertarian leanings of freethought groups; sources are silent.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; secular feminists are divided between harm-reduction and protective views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Freethought tradition prizes open criticism of religion, so adherents lean against speech restrictions, though feminists split over harassment; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Inferred: a movement built on dissent and equal rights is hostile to bypassing legislatures.

state-harmful.rationale: Atheist feminists seek state action on rights, so reject the claim the state is unnecessary; inferred.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the generally progressive US secular-feminist milieu; sources are silent.

empower-police-military.rationale: Inferred: little in the sources, and the progressive milieu leans against expanding police power.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Secular feminists are famously split between abolitionist and sex-work-rights positions.

decide-locally.rationale: Gage and Stanton sought national constitutional guarantees for women over state-level laws; mild inference.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the reform-minded progressive tradition; not discussed in the sources.

traditional-family.rationale: Stanton and Gage attacked the Bible- and canon-law-based subordination of wives in marriage, so adherents reject the claim that traditional family structure is the foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Hutchinson argues gay rights are civil rights and attacks conservative church leaders who condemn same-sex marriage and deny gay couples marital benefits; Gupta names religious opposition to gay marriage as an attack on equality.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anne Gaylor wrote Abortion Is a Blessing, ran abortion referral and funding, and founded FFRF because she saw religion as root of women's oppression.

more-religion-public.rationale: Gage opposed Bible in schools and Sabbath laws, and FFRF litigates against religion in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Modern atheist feminism, as in Hutchinson's work, challenges secular movements to confront institutional racism, rejects colorblindness and campaigns against racially disproportionate school discipline.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Stanton argued women's inferiority came from men and tradition rather than divine nature, implying roles are social; modern view is inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Atheist feminists see tradition as a vehicle for patriarchy and religion; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Stanton called compromise 'cowardice' and demanded that churches change their creeds now.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from the progressive milieu; not addressed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: international women's rights instruments appeal to feminists; sources silent.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; no consistent adherent position.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from universalist rights language of feminism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No source ties atheist feminism to a view on foreign force; some adherents cite women's rights abuses as grounds for intervention while others oppose war, so the movement is split.

open-borders.rationale: The sources say nothing on borders; secular feminists divide between cosmopolitan and restrictionist positions, so neutral.

limit-growth.rationale: The atheist feminist literature in the sources never discusses economic growth or the environment, and no adherent consensus exists.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the science-respecting, progressive orientation; sources silent.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; science-friendly but not techno-optimist as such.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear energy is not part of the movement's concerns in any source consulted, and secular feminists hold varied views.

revolution-justified.rationale: Stanton pursued persuasion, law and critique rather than revolution; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not addressed; respect for science balanced by democratic commitments.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred; the sources do not discuss economic systems.

socialized-markets.rationale: Neither Stanton, Gage nor FFRF addresses how firms should be owned, so no position can be derived beyond neutrality.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is untouched by the sources; nothing in the ideology's principles favours or opposes a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Nineteenth-century feminists attacked inheritance rules favouring sons, but taxation is not discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Feminists are divided on unconditional income, some seeing it as recognising unpaid care and others fearing it entrenches women's domestic role, and the sources are silent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the cosmopolitan outlook; not addressed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is outside the sources, and no principle of atheist feminism bears on it.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Gage and Stanton fought for women's property rights, but nothing says property should be dispersed among small owners, so neutral.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that adherents want women paid wages, not their abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream outlook.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from liberal individual-rights outlook.

one-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: a dissent-based freethought movement rejects single-party ideological rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Gage attacked rule by church and hereditary authority; mild inference.

democracy-best.rationale: Gage and Stanton fought for the vote as a natural right and for women's participation in self-government.

direct-votes.rationale: The sources stress women's access to the vote, not the choice between direct and representative lawmaking.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as a basis of power are not discussed; the movement's reliance on constitutional rights and litigation suggests mild disagreement.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is not discussed; the movement's emphasis on uniform national rights for women suggests mild disagreement.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred: Stanton and Gage rejected the doctrine that women are created inferior to men, a narrower claim than the statement about natural rulers in general.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; historical movement was nonviolent but no stated principle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Atheist feminism descends from reform and humanitarian movements that did not glorify war; this is inferred from that outlook.

separate-church-state.rationale: Gage argued Church and State together subordinated women and held the country to be political, not religious.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Stanton rejected divine authorship of the Mosaic code and Gage condemned theological laws subjugating women.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: reliance on state-guaranteed legal rights.

military-superiority.rationale: Nothing in the sources concerns great-power rivalry; a mild disagreement is inferred from the movement's humanist, rights-first outlook.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Modern atheist feminism claims universal equality of persons, so a nation of one ethnic group is inconsistent with it; inferred, not stated in sources.

class-struggle-history.rationale: These feminists see patriarchy and religion, not class, as the central axis; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; feminists split on outcomes versus opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Gage defended Iroquois sovereignty and treaty rights, so tilt supportive; modern application inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are not addressed in the sources, and adherents' views on historic wrongs vary.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; humanist ethics lean against it.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from Stanton's and Gage's assertion of women's individual rights against church and community authority; they did not address duties versus rights in general.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The environment is not part of the sources; a naturalistic worldview neither requires nor excludes intrinsic value in nature.

limit-population.rationale: Gaylor ran a ZPG referral service, but voluntary choice rather than state limits is the stance; neutral.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' commitment to science and reason makes agreement unlikely, so mild disagreement is inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources do not discuss technology policy; science-friendliness does not imply wanting institutions disrupted, so neutral.

human-enhancement.rationale: Not addressed; secular feminists generally defend bodily autonomy but no source applies it to enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's commitment to women's participation in self-government suggests mild disagreement with handing decisions to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from civil-liberties leanings; sources silent.

restore-past-order.rationale: Both Stanton and Gage portray the past order as one of women's subjection under church and state.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The sources do not address pragmatism versus principle; Stanton's insistence on principle over compromise cuts against it but not decisively.

direct-action.rationale: Historical campaigns used lecturing, litigation and lobbying; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources do not state a view on prefigurative methods, so neutral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The rationalist, progress-oriented tradition of Stanton and Gage makes agreement implausible, though not discussed directly.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Stanton and Gage attacked the sexual division of roles, but not the division of labor generally, so neutral.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need is not discussed; adherents range across liberal and socialist positions.

production-for-use.rationale: Economic organisation is not addressed in the sources; no consensus among adherents.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist exploitation theory is not part of the sources, which centre on religion and sex rather than class.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A movement built on free dissent and individual rights has no reason to accept class dictatorship; inferred.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural organisation is outside the sources; mild disagreement inferred from the individual-rights emphasis.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The sources concern religion and patriarchy, not imperialism, and the claim is a Marxist thesis that adherents do not generally share.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement seeks state action and public funding for rights and services, so it rejects the libertarian claim; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Freethought tradition favours liberty except harm; inferred, as the sources do not state it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not addressed, and feminists split over group rights.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' emphasis on bodily autonomy and consent suggests mild disagreement.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement fought to win women the vote, which makes voting central, so a strong rejection of exit over voice is inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers contradicts the rights-and-citizenship framing used by Gage and Stanton; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred from feminist concern with material means to act.

media-academia-power.rationale: The claim is a populist-right thesis that adherents do not share; mild disagreement is inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Gage was an abolitionist; modern adherents reject racial hierarchies; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Gage and Stanton demanded individual votes for women, so representing people through families and bodies instead of as individuals is inconsistent; inferred.

total-state.rationale: A movement defending individual liberty of conscience and women's rights opposes total state control; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is progressive and cosmopolitan, so a radical national rebirth narrative is rejected by inference.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; the humanist, rights-based outlook implies rejection of expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority based on personal oaths of loyalty is a feudal pattern that Gage and Stanton's equal-rights arguments reject; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Gage was an abolitionist who sheltered fugitives, so legal bondage to land is contrary to her stated principles.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Stanton appealed to critical reason and 'truth' on scripture; later feminist standpoint views split.

universal-morality.rationale: Nasrin holds that universal human rights apply to every culture and rejects an Islamic declaration of human rights and cultural defences of practices harmful to women; adherents ground this in reason rather than revelation.

single-common-good.rationale: Atheist feminists argue that a supposed common good has historically meant men's interests and that women's interests must be represented separately; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and atheist feminists are divided on Zionism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents' views vary with their stance on particular conflicts.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival policy is wholly outside the sources, so neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; adherents vary between liberal and socialist economic views.

school-vouchers.rationale: Vouchers can fund religious schools, and Gage and FFRF oppose religion in public education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed; progressive-leaning adherents probably accept stimulus, so mild disagreement is inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not link political freedom to economic freedom; feminist emphasis on women's material dependence suggests scepticism.

rule-by-example.rationale: Stanton and Gage demanded enforceable laws and rights for women instead of relying on moral exemplars, so government by example alone is rejected; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents' views differ.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; the internationalist, rights-based outlook suggests mild disagreement with unilateral force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Atheism is definitional here, and Stanton insisted the Bible be read critically rather than revered, calling it a fetish.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The universal-rights outlook suggests opposing citizenship restrictions on welfare; inferred only.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Feminists commonly oppose work requirements that ignore unpaid care labour; inferred, not stated in the sources.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class relations are not discussed in the sources; neutral.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Gage's histories show reverence for recording the past, and the movement values libraries and records, so a sacrifice of heritage is rejected; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: A front organised against Western powers is not a concern of the movement, which pursues universal women's rights; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organise nationally or internationally is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Stanton and Gage rejected the idea that women are by creation subordinate and confined to a 'divinely ordained sphere'.

ban-interest.rationale: A ban on interest comes from religious law, which atheist feminists oppose as a basis for legislation; inferred from that principle.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Gage was an abolitionist and the movement claims equal rights for all persons, so racial segregation is rejected; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Feminists here treat state as patriarchal and church-linked, less as class tool; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed; the progressive, science-trusting milieu suggests mild disagreement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Adherents seek freedom of belief and practice, so forcing cultural assimilation is mildly rejected; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: This is a conspiracy theory, and the movement's rationalist commitments imply rejection; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; PR is associated with higher female representation, so mild agreement is inferred from the movement's aims.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a national form of government is not a concern of the movement; the universalist humanist outlook implies rejection.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Stanton and Gage argued church and state structurally subordinated women to men, and modern atheist feminism treats religion as a source of this.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The sources attack clergy and law for subordinating women but do not make general claims about political corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion violates the bodily autonomy central to the movement's reproductive rights stance; inferred from Gaylor's advocacy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; accountability for abuses fits a rights-based outlook, so mild agreement is inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Atheist feminism looks to the state for rights, healthcare access and anti-discrimination law, so a minimal state is rejected; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The movement claims equal moral worth for all persons and Gage was an abolitionist, so this is rejected; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Stanton cited the equal dominion of man and woman in Genesis and Gage condemned teaching that women are not created equal as the 'most grievous wrong'.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist strategy debates fall outside the sources; neutral.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed directly; Gage's defence of Native peoples is only a weak guide.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Nasrin wants sharia abolished, not modified, in favour of a uniform civil code not based on religious dogma, and says that where religious laws exist women cannot get equal rights.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from the defence of the right to leave religion, as in Nasrin's case; laws restricting conversion between religions are not addressed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: This is a religion-motivated prohibition, and atheist feminists oppose enacting religious rules into law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Gage opposed Bible instruction in schools, and FFRF won a case ending Christian doctrine teaching in a public school.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A growing state under siege is not part of the movement's concerns; the liberal rights outlook implies disagreement.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Woman's Bible quotes 'No just government can be formed without the consent of the governed' and asks why women should obey laws they never consented to; Gage likewise calls consent the question in which woman is most deeply concerned.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals are not addressed, so neutral.

population-transfer.rationale: Forcing minorities out violates the equal-rights principle on which the movement rests; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: No source states a non-aggression principle, and the movement supports state enforcement of rights, so neutral.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The movement's tradition of reform and cooperative rights advocacy does not rest on struggle between peoples; mild disagreement inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Freethought liberals are divided between free expression and defending the constitutional order, and the sources are silent.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Stanton's critique of women's subjection to men's arbitrary authority fits non-domination, but she did not use the concept.

separated-powers.rationale: Gage's separation of church and state is a form of checking power; wider constitutional design inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement relies on open persuasion, lecturing and litigation rather than a disciplined revolutionary party; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not addressed directly; the sources focus on women's status rather than on a priority for the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure is outside the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Mild disagreement inferred from the progressive and pro-labour milieu; the sources do not address strikes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Gaylor promoted voluntary family planning, but attributing poverty to population over institutions is not part of the sources; mild disagreement inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: the movement claims equal worth for all and Gage allied women's rights with abolition and Native rights, so diversity is not seen as a threat.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is outside the sources; no principle bears on it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The movement's reliance on legal rights protections suggests resistance to suspending them; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not addressed anywhere in the sources.

party-controls-media.rationale: A freethought movement depends on a free press to criticise religion, so state control of media is rejected; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party command of the army is alien to a liberal rights movement; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not addressed; mild disagreement inferred from the universalist outlook.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no principle of the ideology bears on it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party decisions conflict with the freethinking individualism of the movement; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational union is not a topic in the sources, and adherents have no common view.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of forces is not discussed; the preference for legislatures and constitutional limits suggests mild disagreement.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Stanton blamed clergy and bishops as bitter enemies of woman and opposed hierarchy over women; church governance not addressed directly.

clerical-rule.rationale: Gage argued Church-State union kept women subordinate and attacked clerical dominion as the cause.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is not defined by a stance on wartime loyalty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Freethought tradition opposes moral censorship; inferred from movement aims.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The movement favours limits on entrenched power, so unlimited re-election is mildly rejected; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall is not discussed in the sources, so neutral.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are outside the sources, and adherents are split.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compulsory home ownership has no basis in the sources; inferred rejection.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing the army with an armed citizenry is not part of the movement; inferred disagreement from gun-control leanings.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nothing links the movement to romantic ruralism, and urban centres were its base; inferred disagreement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Border questions are outside the sources.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement values education, and Stanton and Gage were highly educated reformers; the populist claim is rejected by inference.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Gupta says all religions do not have the same respect for human rights and Nasrin rejects cultural defences of practices harmful to women, so adherents judge customs by how they treat women.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the progressive secular milieu generally opposes capital punishment, so mild disagreement.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Hutchinson's Women's Leadership Project brings a feminist secular curriculum into high schools, training students in sexual-assault prevention, HIV/AIDS education, reproductive justice and gender equality.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: FFRF litigates against religious teaching in public schools and Gage opposed Bible instruction there.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Secular feminists are historically split on pornography.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship is not addressed; the equal-rights outlook suggests mild disagreement.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Adherents want religion barred from privileged treatment, and Gupta wants faith not shielded from criticism or secular law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The statement echoes Mill, and a freethought movement that prizes nonconformity probably agrees mildly, though no source says so.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no principle bears directly on it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anti-colonial economic transformation is outside the sources.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional drafting procedure is not addressed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Trading freedoms for growth contradicts the liberty emphasis of freethought; inferred disagreement.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed directly; humanist universalism makes mild agreement likely.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear policy is outside the sources; the humanist, anti-militarist leaning suggests mild disagreement.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The method of choosing a head of state is not discussed.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; a mild lean against inflexible territorial claims is inferred from the rights-based outlook.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The sources do not treat property theory beyond women's property rights, so neutral.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A Marxist theoretical debate outside the sources.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is not addressed; adherents hold varied views.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation disputes are not addressed in the sources, and adherents have no common view.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Gage and FFRF object to church privileges and entanglement; subordinating clergy to civil authority is plausible but not stated in so many words. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neither ceremonial nor partisan heads are linked to the ideology.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; mild disagreement inferred from the rights outlook.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements such as one country, two systems are outside the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Gage condemns rulers, ecclesiastical and temporal, who claim authority by 'divine right', and a Woman's Bible contributor ties the Bible doctrine of the divine right of kings to men's servility.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation is more compatible with the movement's egalitarian leanings; mild disagreement inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Stanton attributed women's subordination to upbringing, law and teaching rather than innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from Gage's natural-rights case for women; the sources do not discuss whether rulers are bound by law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not a concern of the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-regime theory is not addressed in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Honouring a leader as the embodiment of the nation is contrary to the freethought rejection of reverence; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Feminists are divided on a presumption of equal parenting time and no source addresses it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist-style thesis outside the sources and unconnected to the movement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not addressed in the sources, and adherents vary.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not addressed, and adherents vary by conflict.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on shared nationality contradict the universal-rights outlook; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Atheist feminism holds religion is a source of oppression and defends the right to criticise and leave it; Nasrin is a leading figure persecuted for this.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelling women's dress by religious law is a paradigm of the religious oppression these feminists oppose.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic political unity has no place in the movement's universalist humanism; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority self-government is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's universal-rights approach suggests neutrality on this Jewish-political debate.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stanton and Gage held that ideas and religious teaching shaped women's position, opposing a purely materialist account; mild disagreement inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is not addressed in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not addressed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: rights guarantees for women need protection from majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Opposition to sexism within secular organisations and women-in-secularism efforts imply support for parity; legal requirement is inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs conflict with the cosmopolitan outlook; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; mild agreement inferred from progressive leanings.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives is a socialist-state idea not found in the sources; mild disagreement inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco theory conflicts with the movement's reliance on persuasion and law; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from the attack on inherited, ordained male headship; the sources do not address hereditary titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: A nation-centred history curriculum conflicts with the movement's universalist outlook; mild disagreement inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Gage defended Native sovereignty against forced citizenship, so rule over supposedly less advanced peoples is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching loyalty to flag and anthem is not a movement aim, and rationalist secularists tend to resist indoctrination in schools; mild disagreement inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; progressive leanings suggest mild disagreement with abolishing them.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is outside the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist crisis theory is not part of the sources.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial nostalgia is rejected by the humanist outlook; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory delinking is not addressed in the sources; mild disagreement inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis outside the sources, with mild disagreement inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Opposition to sexism includes anti-discrimination law; inferred from stated aims.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Gage argued women had natural rights, which suggests protection through firm constitutional guarantees; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; Gage's concern for honouring Native treaties does not extend to colonial partition treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Gage insisted on government by consent through voting, which includes women.

minority-veto.rationale: A single dissenter's veto conflicts with democratic rule that the movement sought to extend to women; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to rulers is not addressed in the sources, and movement history favoured peaceful agitation.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The sources do not discuss parliamentary supremacy; Gage's emphasis on constitutional rights could cut either way.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Humanist ethics generally grant animals moral standing, but the sources do not discuss it.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed, and adherents range from vegetarian to humane-use views.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Stanton and Gage demanded rights rather than paternalistic charity from the privileged; mild disagreement inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Stanton urged women to press legislators, churches and revising committees, the opposite of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school style critique is outside the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not part of the sources, though Stanton's critique of church teaching resembles it; neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: World-systems theory is outside the sources.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving offices for the native-born conflicts with the equal-rights outlook; inferred.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal communist-movement dispute outside the sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not addressed, so mild disagreement inferred only from humanist internationalism.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist claims conflict with the movement's rights-based outlook; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Gage defended Native nations' sovereignty but did not argue for rule over settlers, so neutral.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, but mild agreement is inferred from liberal humanist commitments.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The Cold War equivalence thesis is outside the sources, and adherents' views differ.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Gage's abolitionism implies slavery was central; inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; progressive-leaning adherents lean against preserving monuments to condemned figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and feminists are divided over whether men's issues deserve equal programmes.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Feminism treats violence against women as structurally rooted; claim of symmetry is resisted, though not stated. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Nasrin's insistence that universal human rights bind every culture; the sources speak of rights, not of forms of government.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for the military is alien to a civilian rights movement; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Feminist tradition supports this, but not stated in the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Lifelong filial duty belongs to religious-traditional ethics which the movement criticises; mild disagreement inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not addressed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and no principle of the ideology bears on foreign ownership of strategic firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Gage held a woman could free herself from an adulterous husband and both attacked church control of marriage.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is not addressed in the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private pension accounts disadvantage women with interrupted careers, a standard feminist objection, though not in the sources; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Occupancy-and-use tenure is an anarchist idea outside the sources; mild disagreement inferred given Gage's stress on property rights for women.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

single-official-language.rationale: Mandatory monolingualism is not a movement concern; mild disagreement inferred from freedom-of-expression commitments.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; the cosmopolitan outlook suggests mild disagreement.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate impact doctrine is not addressed in the sources, and adherents vary.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Critique of consumerism is not part of the sources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; the humanist outlook suggests mild disagreement.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Cold War bloc discipline conflicts with self-determination and rights; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mild agreement inferred from the progressive milieu.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; restrictions often target rights groups, so mild disagreement is inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred from Gage's condemnation of enforced motherhood; financial incentives to have children are not addressed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; mild disagreement inferred from the equal-rights outlook.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employer-of-last-resort policy is outside the sources and adherents are split.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and adherents hold varied views.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Stanton urged defying church authority but the sources do not state a general moral theory of obedience to law.

non-intervention.rationale: Gage and Stanton emphasised universal rights, which implies external concern for abuses; mild disagreement with absolute non-intervention inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy beliefs about minorities conflict with the movement's rationalism and equal-rights stance; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Stanton and Gage criticised marriage as bondage under religious law, not marriage itself; reform rather than abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed; mild agreement inferred from the freethought commitment to open inquiry.

informal-organisation.rationale: Adherents built formal organisations such as FFRF; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; mild disagreement inferred because international women's rights norms matter to this movement.

religious-nation.rationale: Church-State union is what Gage and FFRF attack; a nation defined by religion is the opposite.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tribute systems are unrelated to the movement; the rights-based outlook implies rejection.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional fiscal policy is outside the sources; mild disagreement inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed; neutral because the distinction between personal and productive property is a socialist formulation outside the sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views on Cold War stances.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Health-system delivery models are not addressed in the sources.

religion-illusion.rationale: Atheists agree religion is mistaken, but atheist feminists hold religion actively oppresses women rather than merely consoles, and do not expect it to fade by itself.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Marxist formulation is not part of the sources; adherents split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Stanton and Gage focused on law, religion and the vote rather than economic transformation; adherents split.

socialized-care.rationale: Socialised housework is a socialist feminist demand not found in the sources; adherents split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is unrelated to the movement; mild disagreement inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Gage called on government to honour Native treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small commune ideals are not part of the sources; mild disagreement inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement to alter demographics conflicts with equal rights; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-position economics is not addressed in the sources.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Claims based on historical or religious ties conflict with the secular, rights-based outlook; mild disagreement inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The movement stresses reason and evidence, so denial is rejected; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Hutchinson treats gay rights as civil rights against religious condemnation of homosexuality, and Gupta counts religious campaigns against gay people's rights as attacks on equality.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppression of dissent contradicts freethought and free speech values; inferred.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Gupta defends the right to stand against religion, and Nasrin is a leading figure persecuted under blasphemy-type law.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial exploitation is rejected by the equal-rights outlook; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious duty of armed resistance is contrary to the movement's secularism; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Takfiri doctrine is anathema to a movement opposing religion in politics; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed directly, though extending political participation to women was the central aim; mild agreement inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Hutchinson writes that oppression and privilege intersect across identities and calls for a civil rights movement based on intersectionality; Gage linked abolition, Native rights and women's rights.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Secular feminists are divided on this, and the sources do not address it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Freethought groups usually back it; not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Adherents are mostly progressive and see the left-right division as meaningful; mild disagreement inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist alienation is not part of the sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Adherents criticise Islam as they do all religions on women's rights, but reject cultural essentialism; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Stanton and Gage rejected divine sanction for male authority and for Church-State rule.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Strict secularism leads many adherents to want state neutrality in dress, though some feminists dispute this. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the movement's campaign against sexual harassment at atheist events, as in the Watson case; nothing found on nondisclosure agreements or arbitration.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed; mild agreement inferred from the progressive social-democratic milieu.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not addressed; adherents do not generally seek abolition of armies, so mild disagreement inferred.

rich-first.rationale: The step-by-step enrichment thesis is not addressed; mild disagreement inferred from egalitarian outlook.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Alignment policy is outside the sources.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession conflicts with the movement's attack on inherited authority; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutualist banking is outside the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Austerity conditions are not addressed in the sources, though feminists have criticised austerity's effect on women; neutral.

property-franchise.rationale: Gage treats the recognition of property rather than person in government as a relic of feudal times and claims the vote as a natural right of persons.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is a distinct strand not addressed by the sources.

reification.rationale: The Lukacsian concept is outside the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law theory is not addressed, though Gage's reliance on legal rights is compatible; neutral.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the natural-rights case for suffrage and Gage's abolitionism; the sources here do not address racial limits on the vote.

online-participation.rationale: E-democracy is not addressed in the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data is not discussed in the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Religious limits on marriage are an example of religious control that adherents oppose.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a religious minority is bigotry that conflicts with the movement's equal-rights outlook; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Deliberative mini-publics are not addressed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Stanton wanted the Bible critically reread and revised, but Gupta and Gaylor see religion itself as the root, so adherents split on reform.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents vary on economic views.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, but mild agreement is inferred from opposition to religious sexual morality.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: adherents campaign for keeping religion out of the state, and no source found argues either for or against the state promoting atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Abolitionism is not addressed; mild disagreement inferred since feminists seek state enforcement against violence.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational schemes often entrench religious communities; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Gaylor's funds depended on private charity, but the movement favours public guarantees of rights; mild disagreement inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not addressed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not addressed in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Stanton asked why the church refuses to ordain women, though atheists object to religious office as such; mild agreement.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Stanton rejected marriage as bondage and the husband's headship; Gage opposed wives' loss of control over their bodies.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not addressed in the sources.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not addressed; mild disagreement inferred as authors such as Stanton and Gage lived by publishing.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled youth movements conflict with freethought individualism; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing of nuclear weapons is not addressed in the sources, and no principle of the ideology bears on it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign military bases are outside the sources, and adherents hold no common view.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of past genocides is not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The sources discuss women's labour and property rights but not the principle of rewarding work over ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Gaylor and others do not espouse pacifism, and the sources are silent; mild disagreement inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Gage herself wrote of a lost ancient matriarchate, but a nationalist continuity myth is not part of the movement; mild disagreement.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The sources do not address whether biological sex is constructed, and secular feminists split sharply on it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Modern feminists disagree on whether feminist politics needs a fixed category of women, and the sources do not settle it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Sanctifying the national dead conflicts with the secular outlook; mild disagreement inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement rejects religious framings of politics; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The role of a national homeland for a diaspora is outside the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not part of the sources; the movement's agenda is legal and political change, so mild disagreement inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Atheists do not believe in God, though Stanton showed the male framing of the Deity as man-made; neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Stanton read scripture by whether it exalts woman, but atheist adherents reject scripture's authority altogether; split framing. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic economic nationalism conflicts with equality principles; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Ethnic territorial unification is not addressed in the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though liberal freedoms point toward mild agreement.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate that falls outside the sources.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Public utilities are not addressed in the sources.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not addressed in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Libertarian municipalism is outside the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Communalist confederalism is outside the sources.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: breadwinner model is tied to traditional roles.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulatory speed is not addressed in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, though pseudonymity helps nonbelievers in hostile settings.

person-over-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the individual-rights tradition of Gage and Stanton supports mild agreement.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Atheist feminists reject supernatural claims about human nature; politics not seen as serving a spiritual side.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Devolution design is not addressed in the sources.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural technology is not addressed in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is outside the sources, so neutral.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Organising by race for group interests conflicts with the universalist outlook; mild disagreement inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed; adherents hold varied views, with mild disagreement inferred from the universalist outlook.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not defined by this question.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Linguistic nationalism is not part of the sources; mild disagreement inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Nasreen says politics based on religion is always misogynistic, and Gage opposed any union of church and state; separate religious electorates build religion into politics.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiratorial national-threat narratives conflict with the movement's rationalism; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Tuition is not addressed; mild agreement inferred from progressive leanings.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not addressed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mild agreement inferred from humanist ethics.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Gage argued for the vote as natural right rather than moral difference, but others stress women's values; split. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

arms-reduction.rationale: Disarmament policy is not addressed in the sources.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labour law is not addressed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Binding limits on borrowing are not addressed; mild disagreement inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement works through the existing legal system, so it rejects smashing it; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: A secular movement rejects the sacralisation of the nation; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not addressed; adherents mix universalist and constructionist views.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Atheism denies that religions express any spiritual truth.

ban-fgm.rationale: Nasrin and other adherents oppose religiously justified harm to women; not stated explicitly in sources. None of the cited sources takes up this statement, so this is a low-confidence reading of the general outlook.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Gage listed canon-law limits on wives' property and the movement fought for women's property rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification dispute outside the sources.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Libertarian environmental law is outside the sources.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary authority is typically patriarchal and religious, which the movement opposes; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; mild disagreement inferred from reformist leanings.

voter-id.rationale: Voter ID is not addressed; mild disagreement inferred from the progressive milieu.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Adherents want no religious law precedence at all; mild agreement by the underlying equality.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, so neutral.

premarital-sex.rationale: Rejecting religious sexual morality is core to atheist feminism; Gaylor provided birth-control and abortion access.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Shutdowns restrict free expression, which freethought defends; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Atheist feminism is defined by this claim, which Stanton, Gage and Anne Gaylor each stated.

women-suffrage.rationale: Matilda Joslyn Gage helped found the National Woman Suffrage Association in 1869 and with Elizabeth Cady Stanton led the suffrage movement for years, co-writing the History of Woman Suffrage.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the movement's progressive, science-minded outlook; the sources do not discuss race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: a rights-based secular feminism favours state bodies enforcing equality, but the sources do not discuss them.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The sources are about religion, sex and law, not property origins, so adherents are split.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the movement's rights-based, progressive outlook; the sources do not discuss international courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Stanton's Woman's Bible and Gage's Woman, Church and State treat scripture as a human, male-authored record used to subordinate women.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: a movement demanding women's equality would want it written into any group's self-rule; the sources do not discuss it.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from a progressive rights-based outlook that is suspicious of bureaucratic rule; the sources do not discuss planned economies.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: women's suffrage activists such as Stanton and Gage campaigned for the direct vote; not discussed for higher offices.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement demands strict church-state separation, as in the Freedom From Religion Foundation's case against a state Good Friday holiday and Gage's opposition to church privilege.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; support for group rights competes with opposition to religiously defined communities.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred from the movement's democratic, consent-based outlook; not discussed in the sources.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, so adherents have no settled view.

simple-living.rationale: The sources do not address lifestyle ideals, so adherents are indifferent.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the movement's insistence on equal rights for all citizens; not discussed in the sources.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the movement's commitment to women's legal equality, which implies equal burdens; the sources do not discuss the draft.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: a secular, rights-based movement is wary of sacralised national claims, though it never addresses the question.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from its legal-equality and due-process commitments; killing without trial contradicts them.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: the sources never touch foreign alignment, and adherents have no shared line.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: ethnic-kin protection is a nationalist position at odds with the movement's universalist, secular outlook.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not discuss resource ownership and adherents split between left and liberal views.

self-ownership.rationale: Bodily autonomy and reproductive rights are core, as in Gaylor's work, but the statement's claim to full rights over one's labour is not addressed, so this is inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: no source addresses tax policy and adherents split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred: the progressive outlook favours universal provision, but the sources do not say.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the movement works through organised groups such as the Freedom From Religion Foundation, so bypassing groups runs against its practice.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred: opposition to special legal privileges for religion extends naturally to opposing privileges generally, though businesses are not discussed.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Gage's Woman, Church and State and the FFRF's separation-of-church-and-state work reject any role for religion in public life.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: a movement that treats inherited religious tradition as a source of women's oppression is unlikely to want a return to ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Stanton and Gage attacked church and law for denying women equal rights in marriage, so a wife's ability to divorce without consent follows from their legal-equality case.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address resource sovereignty.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: progressive egalitarian leanings suggest equality of outcome matters, but the sources do not discuss it.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: no source addresses it and adherents have no common position.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: modern figures such as Sikivu Hutchinson centre racism in black secular feminism, but the sources give no direct statement.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: the movement urges reform of unjust laws, but natural-law language is religious in origin and adherents are split on it.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the sources and adherents split.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: the sources never address world order.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the sources and adherents range from liberal to Marxist.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: not addressed, and the movement is split between liberal and socialist outlooks.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the movement is built on challenging sexism and religion, which are identity issues, so it would resist setting them aside.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: the movement's rights-based, secular-liberal outlook is hostile to one-party rule, though it is not discussed.

missingStatements.text: Religious authorities should not control women's marriage, divorce, property or custody through religious law.
missingStatements.rationale: Gage described the Church's control of marriage and canon-law limits on wives' property, and the movement opposes religious personal-status law.

missingStatements.text: Religion is a major cause of women's oppression.
missingStatements.rationale: Atheist feminism is defined by this claim, which Stanton, Gage and Anne Gaylor each stated.

missingStatements.text: Public holidays, prayers and religious displays should not be sponsored by the state.
missingStatements.rationale: FFRF won a case overturning a Wisconsin Good Friday holiday and Gage opposed Sabbath laws.

notes: Strands differ on sex work, pornography, trans inclusion and how far to criticise religious minorities, and there is internal conflict over sexism in the atheist movement. Stanton blamed the church more than Christianity itself, following Lucretia Mott. Deepen pass 2026-10-29 (claude-opus-5-5): searched the full texts of The Woman's Bible and Woman, Church and State for consent, franchise, divine right, wages, prostitution regulation, treaties and schools; read Nasrin, Hutchinson and Gupta on law, sexuality, race and culture. The record says almost nothing on economics, foreign policy, ecology or technology, so those stay low. Gage opposed abortion on principle and state licensing of prostitution, so 19th-century and modern strands differ there. Several earlier medium answers deduced from general values were lowered.
